newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 8.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 8.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Friday:
* The market is likely to trade in a narrow range on lack of compelling, positive news and on concerns over the adverse effects of the peso depreciation over the next six months, traders said.

* "People are still not ready to commit to the market on a longer term basis, but an IMF rescue package for beleaguered Thailand and further cuts in interest rates are just the keys for building investor confidence in the coming days," said Sun Hung Kai Securities in its daily outlook.
* On Thursday, the Philippine composite index fell by 24.78 points to 2,670.01 points.
* The Dow Jones on Thursday ended 71.31 points lower at 8,188.00. PLDT's ADR closed lower by $0/07 at $32 1/2.
* The Philippine peso ended up at 28.46 to a U.S. dollar versus 28.49.

* Foreign banks which were kept out of the Philippine Dealing System after the peso's effective devaluation should be allowed to trade on the system again, a Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP) official said.

* Philippine banks were quoting lower secondary bid and offer rates for Treasury bills on Thursday after the central bank slashed its overnight borrowing rate by two percentage points to 18 percent, dealers said.
* EEI Corp said its unaudited net income for the first half of the year rose to 103.95 million pesos compared with 87.66 million during the same period last year.
* Securities and Exchange Commission chairman Perfecto Yasay said he favoured more non-brokers on the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) board of governors.

* Several analysts downgraded expectations for Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd on Thursday, expressing concern about the returns from the bottler's European operations. The company, analysts said, needed to improve its focus on the region which showed disappointing sales revenue and trading profit growth in half-year results.
* Coca-Cola Amatil said its currency management should minimise any effects from the depreciation of the peso on its full year earnings in calendar 1997.
* Ericsson Telecommunications Inc said it has signed an agreement with Globe Telecom for the installation of 6,200 telephone lines worth $5.2 million.

* First Philippine Holdings Corp said its board approved a share swap with its parent Benpres Holdings Corp. Under the proposed agreement, Benpres will exchange 13.8 million Manila Electric Co shares, or 1.7 percent of the outstanding capital stock of Meralco, for new FPHC A shares.

* Manila Bulletin said quoting central bank governor Gabriel Singson that the foreign exchange market would soon stabilise, not only in the Philippines, but all throughout the region, as financial assistance from multinational institutions pour in.

* Merrill Lynch, in a recent economic report on the Philippines, said it expects the peso to strengthen by five percent or about 27.70 from its present level of 28.50 pesos to a dollar. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
* The Philippine Star said National Economic and Development Authority (NEda) insists that government will meet its economic target this year despite indications of a slowdown.
